question: Quelles sont les obligations de notification des incidents majeurs liés aux TIC ?
ground_truth: Les entités financières déclarent les incidents majeurs liés aux TIC à l'autorité compétente concernée (article 46) au moyen d'une notification initiale puis des rapports prévus au paragraphe 4, en utilisant les modèles visés à l'article 20 ; les établissements de crédit importants les déclarent à l'autorité nationale compétente, qui transmet immédiatement à la BCE, et les États membres peuvent exiger une transmission aux CSIRT. Les cybermenaces importantes peuvent être notifiées à titre volontaire. Lorsqu'un incident majeur a une incidence sur les intérêts financiers des clients, les entités financières les informent sans retard injustifié de l'incident et des mesures prises.
notes: smoke query Q1 (fr_to_fr); ground truth by Claude

question: What information must institutions keep in the register of outsourcing arrangements?

sections: 4. Guidelines on outsourcing > Title III – Governance framework > 11 Documentation

ground_truth: For all existing outsourcing arrangements the register should include at least a reference number; the start, renewal and end dates and notice periods; a description of the outsourced function and data (including whether personal data are involved); a category; the service provider's name, registration number, LEI, address and parent company; the countries where the service is performed and where data are located; whether the function is critical or important and why; for cloud outsourcing the service and deployment models and data storage locations; and the date of the latest criticality assessment. For critical or important functions, additional information is required, such as the entities using the outsourcing, group membership of the provider, the latest risk assessment, the approving body, governing law, audit dates, sub-contractors, substitutability, alternative providers, time-criticality and estimated annual budget cost.
notes: smoke query Q2 (en_to_en); ground truth by Claude

question: Quels ratios minimaux de fonds propres les établissements doivent-ils respecter ?
ground_truth: Institutions shall at all times satisfy a Common Equity Tier 1 capital ratio of 4,5 %, a Tier 1 capital ratio of 6 % and a total capital ratio of 8 %, each expressed as a percentage of the total risk exposure amount (Article 92(1)-(2)).
notes: smoke query Q3 (cross_fr_to_en); ground truth by Claude

question: Which article of the AI Act defines high-risk AI systems?

sections: ANNEX III
ANNEXE III
markers: Article 6 Règles relatives à la classification

ground_truth: Article 6 sets the classification rules for high-risk AI systems: an AI system is high-risk if it is a safety component of, or itself, a product covered by the Union harmonisation legislation in Annex I that requires a third-party conformity assessment (Article 6(1)), and AI systems listed in Annex III are also high-risk (Article 6(2)), unless they do not pose a significant risk of harm (Article 6(3)); an Annex III system that performs profiling of natural persons is always high-risk.
notes: smoke query Q5 (no_rag_baseline); ground truth by Claude

question: Que doit contenir la demande qu'un fournisseur adresse à un organisme notifié pour l'évaluation de la documentation technique de son système d'IA à haut risque, selon l'AI Act ?

sections: ANNEX VII
ANNEXE VII

ground_truth: The application must include the name and address of the provider, a written declaration that the same application has not been lodged with any other notified body, and the technical documentation referred to in Annex IV.

key_facts.fact: not lodged with any other notified body

question: Quand un déployeur enregistre un système d'IA à haut risque dans la base de données de l'UE, quelles informations l'AI Act lui impose-t-il de fournir ?

sections: ANNEX VIII
ANNEXE VIII

ground_truth: Deployers registering a high-risk AI system under Article 49(3) must provide, and keep up to date, their name, address and contact details; those of the person submitting the information on their behalf; the URL of the provider's entry for the AI system in the EU database; a summary of the findings of the fundamental rights impact assessment carried out under Article 27; and, where applicable, a summary of the data protection impact assessment.

key_facts.fact: summary of the fundamental rights impact assessment
URL of the provider's entry in the EU database

notes: rewrite proposed by Claude (5.4-B) - not human-verified (Claude rewrite only)

question: Selon l'AI Act, que doit faire le fournisseur d'un outil d'IA générative pour que les images, sons ou textes qu'il produit puissent être reconnus comme générés par une IA ?

markers: Article 50 Obligations de transparence pour les fournisseurs et les déployeurs de certains systèmes d’IA
Article 50 Transparency obligations for providers and deployers of certain AI systems

ground_truth: Les fournisseurs de systèmes d'IA, y compris de systèmes d'IA à usage général, qui génèrent des contenus de synthèse de type audio, image, vidéo ou texte veillent à ce que les sorties soient marquées dans un format lisible par machine et identifiables comme ayant été générées ou manipulées par une IA. Cette obligation ne s'applique pas lorsque le système remplit une fonction d'assistance pour la mise en forme standard ou ne modifie pas de manière substantielle les données d'entrée, ni lorsque l'utilisation est autorisée par la loi à des fins de prévention ou de détection des infractions pénales.

key_facts.fact: générées ou manipulées par une IA

notes: Article 50(2); the ground truth keeps the two exceptions. rewrite proposed by Claude (5.4-B) - HIGH-RISK verified line by line by Chloe (2026-10-18, side-by-side aid prepared by Claude): matches source

question: Under the CRR, what share of the assets behind French FCT senior units used as covered-bond collateral must be residential mortgages?

markers: Article 129 Exposures in the form of covered bonds

ground_truth: The assets underlying such senior units must, at any time while they are in the cover pool, be at least 90 % composed of residential mortgages combined with any prior liens up to the lesser of the principal amounts due under the units, the principal amounts of the liens, and 80 % of the value of the pledged properties. The units must also qualify for credit quality step 1 and must not exceed 10 % of the nominal amount of the outstanding issue.

key_facts.fact: not more than 10 % of the outstanding issue

notes: Wording of the CRR version in the corpus (FCT units; later amended by the covered bond package - not in the corpus). rewrite proposed by Claude (5.4-B) - HIGH-RISK verified line by line by Chloe (2026-10-18, side-by-side aid prepared by Claude): matches source

question: Under the CRR, which kind of clause prevents a netting agreement from being recognised?

markers: Article 296 Recognition of contractual netting agreements

ground_truth: A contractual netting agreement is recognised only if, among other conditions, the contract contains no clause which, in the event of a counterparty's default, permits the non-defaulting counterparty to make only limited payments, or no payments at all, to the estate of the defaulting party, even if the defaulting party is a net creditor (a 'walk away clause').

key_facts.fact: limited payments or no payments at all

notes: rewrite proposed by Claude (5.4-B) - not human-verified (Claude rewrite only)

question: Selon DORA, quels droits une banque doit-elle conserver dans son contrat avec un prestataire TIC qui soutient des fonctions critiques ou importantes ?
ground_truth: Les contrats de fourniture de services TIC qui soutiennent des fonctions critiques ou importantes devraient permettre l'exercice des droits d'accès, d'inspection et d'audit par l'entité financière ou par un tiers désigné, ainsi que le droit de prendre des copies, pour assurer un suivi permanent des performances du prestataire. L'autorité compétente de l'entité financière devrait aussi pouvoir, moyennant préavis, inspecter et auditer le prestataire tiers de services TIC.
notes: rewrite proposed by Claude (5.4-B) - not human-verified (Claude rewrite only)

question: Selon DORA, quelles conditions supplémentaires s'appliquent lorsqu'une entité financière veut confier ses tests de pénétration fondés sur la menace à ses propres testeurs internes ?

markers: Article 27 Exigences applicables aux testeurs afin de réaliser des tests de pénétration fondés sur la menace

ground_truth: En plus des exigences applicables à tous les testeurs (paragraphe 1), le recours aux testeurs internes doit avoir été approuvé par l'autorité compétente concernée ou par l'autorité publique unique désignée ; l'autorité compétente doit avoir vérifié que l'entité financière dispose de ressources suffisantes et veillé à éviter les conflits d'intérêts pendant la conception et l'exécution du test ; et le fournisseur de renseignements sur les menaces doit être externe à l'entité financière.

key_facts.fact: fournisseur de renseignements sur les menaces externe

notes: Article 27(2). rewrite proposed by Claude (5.4-B) - not human-verified (Claude rewrite only)

question: According to the ACPR's 2020 discussion paper on AI governance, how did bringing machine learning into credit-scoring models change governance?

sections: Juin 2020 Gouvernance des algorithmes d’intelligence artificielle dans le secteur financier Document de réflexion AUTEURS Laurent Dupont, Olivier Fliche, Su Yang Pôle Fintech-Innovation, ACPR > 2.2. Travaux exploratoires > 2.2.2. Thème 2 : Modèles internes en banque et assurance

ground_truth: Les deux scénarios étudiés (un grand groupe bancaire et un cabinet de conseil) ont montré trois impacts de gouvernance : une technicité accrue du processus de validation initiale, la mise en place d'outils de monitoring pour le contrôle interne, et l'intégration de méthodes explicatives afin d'assurer le contrôle permanent ainsi que les missions d'audit.
notes: rewrite proposed by Claude (5.4-B) - not human-verified (Claude rewrite only)

question: Selon le document de l'ACPR de 2020 sur la gouvernance de l'IA, où les superviseurs pourraient-ils être formés à la data science ?

sections: Juin 2020 Gouvernance des algorithmes d’intelligence artificielle dans le secteur financier Document de réflexion AUTEURS Laurent Dupont, Olivier Fliche, Su Yang Pôle Fintech-Innovation, ACPR > ÉVALUATION EMPIRIQUE DU ML > 5.5.2. Enjeux spécifiques aux superviseurs

ground_truth: Pour accompagner l'adaptation des méthodes, outils et données du superviseur, le document évoque une formation en Data Science soit chez le superviseur – ce qui est envisagé au sein de l'ACPR –, soit dans des instituts spécialisés (par exemple dans le domaine de la conformité en banque ou de l'actuariat).

question: Dans l'atelier LCB-FT décrit par l'ACPR, à quelle condition le modèle de ML de la banque génère-t-il une alerte pour une transaction ayant un score élevé ?

sections: Annexes > 8.1. Atelier « LCB-FT » > 8.1.9. Atelier complémentaire

ground_truth: Dans l'atelier complémentaire LCB-FT, un filtre fait qu'une transaction ayant obtenu un score élevé par le modèle de ML ne génère une alerte que si aucune alerte n'a été levée par le moteur de règles métier sur ce même client dans les trois mois précédents. Ces alertes supplémentaires sont envoyées directement au niveau N2.

key_facts.fact: aucune alerte du moteur de règles métier

notes: rewrite proposed by Claude (5.4-B) - not human-verified (Claude rewrite only)

question: Selon les orientations de l'ABE sur l'externalisation, dans quels cas une banque doit-elle toujours considérer une fonction externalisée comme critique ou importante ?

sections: 4. Guidelines on outsourcing > Title II – Assessment of outsourcing arrangements > 4 Critical or important functions

ground_truth: Institutions and payment institutions should always consider a function as critical or important (a) where a defect or failure in its performance would materially impair their continuing compliance with their authorisation conditions or regulatory obligations, their financial performance, or the soundness or continuity of their banking and payment services; (b) when operational tasks of internal control functions are outsourced, unless the assessment shows that a failure would not adversely affect the effectiveness of the internal control function; and (c) when they intend to outsource banking or payment activities to an extent that would require authorisation by a competent authority.
notes: Paragraph 29 of the guidelines: numbered paragraphs can trigger P38 (paragraph number cited as a passage number). The 7b ground truth merged paragraphs 29 and 31. rewrite proposed by Claude (5.4-B) - HIGH-RISK verified line by line by Chloe (2026-10-18, side-by-side aid prepared by Claude): matches source

question: What mapping exercise do the EBA ICT and security risk guidelines expect from financial institutions?

sections: Guidelines on ICT and security risk management > 3.3. ICT and security risk management framework > 3.3.2. Identification of functions, processes and assets

ground_truth: Financial institutions should identify, establish and keep updated a mapping of their business functions, roles and supporting processes, to identify the importance of each and their interdependencies related to ICT and security risks. They should also keep an updated mapping of the information assets supporting those functions and processes, such as ICT systems, staff, contractors, third parties and dependencies on other internal and external systems and processes, so as to manage at least the assets that support their critical business functions.
notes: rewrite proposed by Claude (5.4-B) - not human-verified (Claude rewrite only)

question: Under the EBA loan origination guidelines, how should a bank handle a third-party guarantee on a loan to a company?

sections: 5. Loan origination procedures > 5.2 Assessment of borrower’s creditworthiness > 5.2.6 Lending to medium-sized and large enterprises

ground_truth: If a loan agreement involves any form of guarantee from third parties, institutions should assess the level of protection provided by the guarantee and, if relevant, carry out a creditworthiness assessment of the guarantor, applying the relevant provisions of the guidelines depending on whether the guarantor is a natural person or an enterprise. This assessment should be proportionate to the size of the guarantee relative to the loan and to the type of guarantor.

key_facts.fact: proportionate to the size of the guarantee

notes: rewrite proposed by Claude (5.4-B) - not human-verified (Claude rewrite only)

question: Under the EBA internal governance guidelines, what extra information must a bank be able to give its supervisor about a large loan to a board member?

sections: 4. Guidelines > 12.2 Documentation of loans to members of the management body and their related parties and additional information

ground_truth: For a loan to a member of the management body or their related parties above EUR 200 000, institutions should be able to provide to the competent authority on request: the percentage of the loan, and of all outstanding loans to the same debtor, compared with the sum of Tier 1 and Tier 2 capital and with common equity Tier 1 capital; whether the loan is part of a large exposure; and the relative weight of all outstanding loans to that debtor as a percentage of all outstanding loans to members of the management body and their related parties.

key_facts.fact: whether part of a large exposure

question: According to the EBA report on machine learning for IRB models, how does the April 2023 text of the proposed Consumer Credit Directive restrict the data used for creditworthiness assessment?

sections: 5. Interaction with (non-CRR) regulatory frameworks > 5.1 Interaction with GDPR

ground_truth: The April 2023 text of the proposed CCD refers to personal data under Article 9 of the GDPR when prohibiting the use of specific personal data for creditworthiness assessment, also where the data were received from databases located in other Member States. It also prohibits the use of data collected from social networks and refers to the GDPR data minimisation principle in its requirements for assessing consumers' creditworthiness.
notes: rewrite proposed by Claude (5.4-B) - not human-verified (Claude rewrite only)

question: Que recommande l'ABE d'éviter pour que les modèles NI fondés sur le machine learning ne deviennent pas inutilement complexes ?

sections: Annex I– Principle-based recommendations Recommendations regarding the regulatory compliant use of ML techniques in the context of the IRB framework

ground_truth: Institutions are recommended to balance model performance and explainability and to avoid unnecessary complexity that is not justified by a significant improvement in predictive capacity. In particular they should avoid including an excessive number of explanatory drivers or drivers with no significant predictive information, using unstructured data when more conventional data with similar predictive capacity is available, and overly complex modelling choices when simpler approaches give similar results.
notes: rewrite proposed by Claude (5.4-B) - not human-verified (Claude rewrite only)

question: Under the CRR, from what size does an exposure to a client count as a 'large exposure', and what is the maximum it may reach?
ground_truth: An exposure to a client or group of connected clients is a large exposure when its value is equal to or exceeds 10 % of the institution's eligible capital (Article 392). After credit risk mitigation, an institution shall not incur an exposure to a client or group of connected clients exceeding 25 % of its eligible capital (Article 395(1)).
notes: Two articles: definition (392) + limit (395). Q4/P39: the 25 % sits in the first chunk of Article 395. drafted by Claude (5.5-B) - HIGH-RISK re-checked by Claude against SOURCE (2026-10-18); not human-verified

question: What is the maximum fine under the AI Act for a company that puts a social scoring system on the market?
ground_truth: AI systems that evaluate or classify natural persons over time based on their social behaviour or personal characteristics, with the social score leading to detrimental or unfavourable treatment, are prohibited AI practices under Article 5(1)(c). Non- compliance with the Article 5 prohibitions is subject to administrative fines of up to EUR 35 000 000 or, for an undertaking, up to 7 % of its total worldwide annual turnover for the preceding financial year, whichever is higher (Article 99(3)).
notes: Article 5 (what is prohibited) + Article 99 (the fine). drafted by Claude (5.5-B) - HIGH-RISK re-checked by Claude against SOURCE (2026-10-18); not human-verified

question: DORA et les orientations de l'ABE sur l'externalisation imposent toutes deux de tenir un registre : quels accords chaque registre doit-il couvrir, et à quels niveaux ?

sections: 4. Guidelines on outsourcing > Title III – Governance framework > 11 Documentation requirements

ground_truth: DORA (article 28, paragraphe 3) impose aux entités financières de tenir et mettre à jour, au niveau de l'entité et aux niveaux sous-consolidé et consolidé, un registre d'informations sur tous les accords contractuels portant sur l'utilisation de services TIC fournis par des prestataires tiers de services TIC. Les orientations de l'ABE (paragraphe 52) demandent un registre à jour de tous les accords d'externalisation, au niveau de l'établissement et, le cas échéant, aux niveaux sous-consolidé et consolidé, en distinguant l'externalisation de fonctions critiques ou importantes des autres accords et en conservant les accords terminés pendant une période appropriée.
notes: Cross-work DORA (FR) + EBA GL 2019/02 (EN). Same section as smoke Q2, different paragraph (52 vs 54). drafted by Claude (5.5-B) - not human-verified

question: L'AI Act classe le scoring de crédit des particuliers comme à haut risque : selon l'ABE, cela s'applique-t-il aussi aux modèles NI utilisés pour calculer les exigences de fonds propres ?

sections: ANNEX III
ANNEXE III
5. Interaction with (non-CRR) regulatory frameworks > 5.2 Interaction with AI Act > 5.2.1 Clarification on the scope of application of the AI Act

ground_truth: AI systems intended to evaluate the creditworthiness of natural persons or establish their credit score are listed as high-risk in Annex III (point 5(b)), except those used to detect financial fraud. In its 2023 report, the EBA's view is that the high-risk scope should cover only systems used for creditworthiness assessment and credit scoring of natural persons at loan origination, and therefore does not apply directly to other parts of the credit process such as IRB models used to calculate capital requirements; however, the AI Act may still affect IRB models indirectly through the prudential use- test requirement.
notes: Cross-work AI Act + EBA ML report; the question is FR, both sources are EN (EBA part is cross-lingual). Yes/no framing is followed by the reason: the answer must give the EBA view + the indirect effect. drafted by Claude (5.5-B) - not human-verified

question: Which business areas did the ACPR's 2020 exploratory work on AI cover, and what levels of explanation does the paper propose?

sections: Juin 2020 Gouvernance des algorithmes d’intelligence artificielle dans le secteur financier Document de réflexion AUTEURS Laurent Dupont, Olivier Fliche, Su Yang Pôle Fintech-Innovation, ACPR > 1. Résumé

Juin 2020 Gouvernance des algorithmes d’intelligence artificielle dans le secteur financier Document de réflexion AUTEURS Laurent Dupont, Olivier Fliche, Su Yang Pôle Fintech-Innovation, ACPR > PRINCIPE D’EXPLICABILITÉ > 3.4.7. Exemples de niveaux d’explication par cas d’usage > Cas d'usage Critères d'explicabilité Niveau d'explication requis Fonctionnalité de Audience de Domaine Processus métier l'IA l'explication Contexte Risque associé

ground_truth: Les travaux exploratoires couvraient trois domaines : la lutte contre le blanchiment et le financement du terrorisme (LCB-FT), les modèles internes et en particulier le scoring de crédit, et la protection de la clientèle. Le document propose quatre niveaux d'explication, par exigence croissante : 1. observation, 2. justification, 3. approximation, 4. réplication ; le niveau exigible dépend notamment de l'audience visée et du risque associé.

question: Selon DORA, à quelle fréquence les entités financières doivent-elles tester leurs systèmes TIC critiques, et à quelle fréquence pour les tests de pénétration fondés sur la menace ?
ground_truth: Les entités financières, autres que les microentreprises, soumettent au moins une fois par an tous les systèmes et applications de TIC qui soutiennent des fonctions critiques ou importantes à des tests appropriés (article 24, paragraphe 6). Les entités identifiées par l'autorité compétente effectuent au moins tous les trois ans des tests avancés au moyen d'un test de pénétration fondé sur la menace ; l'autorité compétente peut demander de réduire ou d'augmenter cette fréquence selon le profil de risque (article 26, paragraphe 1).

key_facts.fact: au moins une fois par an
au moins tous les trois ans

notes: S18 (Article 27(2), internal testers) is a different provision. drafted by Claude (5.5-B) - not human-verified

question: What do the EBA loan origination guidelines expect from banks that use automated or innovative models to decide on credit?

sections: 4. Internal governance for credit granting and monitoring > 4.3 Credit risk policies and procedures > 4.3.3 Technology-enabled innovation for credit granting
4. Internal governance for credit granting and monitoring > 4.3 Credit risk policies and procedures > 4.3.4 Models for creditworthiness assessment and credit decision-making

ground_truth: When using technology-enabled innovation for credit granting, institutions should capture its risks in their risk management and control frameworks, ensure the management body understands it, understand the models (capabilities, assumptions, limitations, traceability, auditability, robustness), ensure models are fit for purpose (considering an interpretable model when explanations are needed), detect and prevent bias, and continuously monitor model performance (paragraph 53). When using automated models for creditworthiness assessment and credit decisions, they should understand the models and have policies to detect and prevent bias and ensure input data quality, measures for traceability, auditability, robustness and resilience, regular assessment of output quality including backtesting, and control mechanisms, model overrides and escalation procedures, together with adequate model documentation (paragraphs 54-55).
notes: drafted by Claude (5.5-B) - not human-verified

question: D'après les orientations de l'ABE sur la gouvernance interne et sur l'externalisation, qui reste responsable des activités externalisées, et que doit prévoir la politique d'externalisation ?

sections: 4. Guidelines > 8 Outsourcing policy32
4. Guidelines on outsourcing > Title III – Governance framework > 6 Sound governance arrangements and outsourcing

ground_truth: The outsourcing of functions cannot result in the delegation of the management body's responsibilities: institutions remain fully responsible and accountable for complying with all their regulatory obligations, and the outsourcing policy must make clear that outsourcing does not relieve the institution of its regulatory obligations and its responsibilities to its customers. The outsourcing policy, approved and regularly reviewed by the management body, should consider the impact and risks of outsourcing (operational, including legal and IT, reputational and concentration risks) and include reporting and monitoring arrangements from inception to the end of an arrangement, including the business case, contract, implementation, contingency plans and exit strategies; it should also cover intragroup outsourcing and not hinder effective supervision.

key_facts.fact: cannot delegate the management body's responsibilities

notes: Cross-work EBA GL 2021/05 + 2019/02; cross-lingual (FR question, EN sources). drafted by Claude (5.5-B) - not human-verified

question: Que dit l'article 14 de l'AI Act ?
ground_truth: L'article 14 (contrôle humain) exige que les systèmes d'IA à haut risque soient conçus et développés de manière à pouvoir être effectivement contrôlés par des personnes physiques pendant leur utilisation, afin de prévenir ou de réduire au minimum les risques pour la santé, la sécurité ou les droits fondamentaux. Les mesures de contrôle sont proportionnées aux risques, au niveau d'autonomie et au contexte d'utilisation, intégrées par le fournisseur ou mises en œuvre par le déployeur. Les personnes chargées du contrôle doivent notamment pouvoir comprendre les capacités et limites du système, rester conscientes du biais d'automatisation, interpréter correctement les sorties, décider de ne pas utiliser le système ou d'ignorer, remplacer ou inverser sa sortie, et interrompre son fonctionnement.
notes: drafted by Claude (5.5-B) - not human-verified

question: What does Article 30 of DORA require?
ground_truth: L'article 30 (principales dispositions contractuelles) exige que les droits et obligations de l'entité financière et du prestataire tiers de services TIC soient définis clairement et consignés dans un document écrit unique incluant les accords de niveau de service. Les contrats comportent au moins une description des services et des conditions de sous-traitance, les lieux de fourniture des services et de traitement des données, des dispositions sur la protection des données et sur l'accès, la récupération et la restitution des données, les niveaux de service, l'assistance en cas d'incident TIC, la coopération avec les autorités, les droits de résiliation et les préavis. Pour les services soutenant des fonctions critiques ou importantes, des éléments supplémentaires sont exigés, notamment des niveaux de service détaillés avec objectifs de performance, des obligations de notification, des plans d'urgence testés et des mesures de sécurité des TIC.
notes: Cross-lingual (EN question, FR-only DORA). drafted by Claude (5.5-B) - not human-verified

question: What does CRR Article 395 say?
ground_truth: Article 395 limits large exposures: after credit risk mitigation, an institution shall not incur an exposure to a client or group of connected clients exceeding 25 % of its eligible capital. Where the client is an institution, the limit is 25 % of eligible capital or EUR 150 million, whichever is higher (and then within a reasonable limit set by the institution, not above 100 % of eligible capital). EBA was to issue guidelines on limits to exposures to shadow banking entities.

question: Comment l'AI Act traite-t-il un produit d'IA civil réutilisé ensuite à des fins militaires ou de sécurité nationale ?
ground_truth: An AI system placed on the market for civilian or law enforcement purposes that is used, with or without modification, for military, defence or national security purposes does not fall within the scope of the AI Act, whatever the type of entity carrying out those activities. question: How does the AI Act define an 'AI system'?
ground_truth: An AI system is a machine-based system designed to operate with varying levels of autonomy, that may exhibit adaptiveness after deployment, and that, for explicit or implicit objectives, infers from the input it receives how to generate outputs such as predictions, content, recommendations or decisions that can influence physical or virtual environments.

question: What does the CRR require a bank to do to be sure its financial collateral can actually be enforced?
ground_truth: Institutions must fulfil any contractual and statutory requirements and take all steps necessary to ensure the enforceability of the collateral arrangements under the law applicable to their interest in the collateral. question: Under the CRR large exposure rules, what extra own funds charge applies when a trading book exposure has exceeded the limit for no more than 10 days?

markers: Article 397 Calculating additional own funds requirements for large exposures in the trading book

ground_truth: Where the excess has not persisted for more than 10 days, the additional own funds requirement is 200 % of the requirements on the components selected under paragraph 1 (the components of the trading exposure that attract the highest specific-risk requirements). From 10 days after the excess, the components are allocated to Table 1 and multiplied by factors from 200 % up to 900 % depending on the size of the excess.

question: Which kinds of financial firms does DORA leave out because they are already exempt or only lightly regulated under their sector rules?
ground_truth: Les gestionnaires de fonds d'investissement alternatifs visés à l'article 3, paragraphe 2, de la directive 2011/61/UE, les entreprises d'assurance et de réassurance visées à l'article 4 de la directive 2009/138/CE et les institutions de retraite professionnelle gérant des régimes de retraite qui, ensemble, n'ont pas plus de quinze affiliés au total ne sont pas incluses dans le champ d'application de DORA, car ce ne serait pas proportionné. question: When outsourcing, what must a bank do so that it does not become an 'empty shell', according to the EBA outsourcing guidelines?

question: Under the EBA internal governance guidelines, which banks have to set up risk, nomination and remuneration committees?

question: How often do DORA and the EBA ICT and security risk guidelines require the ICT risk management framework to be reviewed?

question: What do DORA and the EBA outsourcing guidelines each require so that a bank can leave a critical ICT or outsourcing provider without disruption?

sections: 4. Guidelines on outsourcing > Title III – Governance framework > 15 Exit strategies

ground_truth: DORA (Article 28(8)) requires exit strategies for ICT services supporting critical or important functions, so that financial entities can exit contracts without disrupting their activities, limiting compliance with regulatory requirements, or harming the continuity and quality of services to clients; exit plans must be comprehensive, documented, sufficiently tested and periodically reviewed, with alternative solutions and transition plans. The EBA guidelines (paragraphs 106-107) require a documented exit strategy for critical or important functions covering termination, provider failure, deterioration of quality and material risks, and the ability to exit without undue disruption, through comprehensive, documented and sufficiently tested exit plans and transition plans to alternative providers or back in-house.

question: Quelles exigences de liquidité à court et à long terme le CRR prévoit-il pour les établissements ?
ground_truth: Under Article 412 (liquidity coverage requirement), institutions shall hold liquid assets whose value covers liquidity outflows less inflows under stressed conditions, so that their liquidity buffers are adequate to face any imbalance under gravely stressed conditions over a period of thirty days. Under Article 413 (stable funding), institutions shall ensure that long-term obligations are adequately met with a diversity of stable funding instruments under both normal and stressed conditions. In this version of the CRR, the detailed provisions of Titles II and III apply exclusively for the purpose of specifying reporting obligations (Article 415).

question: Que prévoit l'article 501 du CRR ?
ground_truth: Article 501 provides that capital requirements for credit risk on exposures to SMEs are multiplied by the factor 0,7619 (the SME supporting factor). The exposure must be in the retail, corporate or secured-by-immovable-property classes (defaulted exposures excluded), the SME is defined by Commission Recommendation 2003/361/EC using only annual turnover, and the total amount owed by the client or group of connected clients (excluding claims secured on residential property) must not exceed EUR 1,5 million. Institutions report SME exposures to competent authorities every three months.
